annotations.text:
B4 - SCROLL-ZOOM, built from your note

Four camera stops: the whole window, the sidebar, one status dot, then gt list. It pulls back out at the end so the detail has somewhere to land.

The recreation is DOM and real text rather than a bitmap, so it stays sharp at 4x - that is the whole reason to rebuild rather than crop a screenshot. Same drift risk as the replica: re-measure it against the app each release.

Dials above the board: stop (auto, or pin any one) and dwell. Pin a stop and drag dwell to feel the pacing.

Stop 02 is the argument for the whole idea. The status dot is seven pixels in the real app and it is the entire product; the only way to make that land is to show it at seven hundred.

D1 - DECRYPT REVEAL, the pick of the three canvasui ideas

The real capture, rendered as an ASCII cipher. Your cursor decrypts a circle of it and the actual UI comes through; move away and it re-encrypts.

Why this one and not the other two: it solves the problem you named. Most of a terminal screenshot is dead space - as cipher that space becomes texture, and the cursor becomes a spotlight you control. It is also the only one of the three that is about terminals rather than merely rendered on one.

Dials: radius, softness, cell, charset (ascii / blocks / binary / hex), tint, passthrough, scramble, drift.

Not the canvasui component - that needs WebGL2 plus the experimental html-in-canvas API and an npm install, none of which survive in a published artifact. This is a canvas-2d rebuild against the real jpg: the cipher layer renders once, only the lens redraws per frame.

Asciify is the same mechanic with the polarity flipped - real page, ASCII lens. Worth trying on the hero rather than here; two lenses on one page is one too many.

Grid is the cut. It is a nice 3D ripple that says nothing about the product.

A · PROPER SNAKE — playable, with sound

Click into the board first, then press I. You get a coin-slot clunk and the two-note chime, the playfield lights up, the scoreboard drops in. WASD or arrows from there. It wraps at the edges, so there is no lose state — a marketing page should never tell a visitor they failed.

One ghost drops off the tail every nine seconds and starts pulsing. Go back for it and you get a rescue chime and a point. That is the whole loop, and it maps onto the product without being cute about it: something wandered off, go collect it.

Ambient until the coin goes in — eight ghosts drifting, pupils tracking a slow point, no HUD, no keycaps. The only tell is the small blinking I in the corner.

The sound here is synthesised placeholder — square waves, about twenty lines. Good enough to judge the timing and the feel. Real ElevenLabs SFX is a separate pass once you like the shape: coin insert, collect, stray, rescue, and probably a low ambient hum.

THE GHOSTS, REDRAWN

You asked to polish them and to back off Pac-Man. Same 4px grid as the app icons, but:

· Solid dome — the old set got its eyes by cutting holes in the silhouette, which is exactly the 1980 sprite. These are closed shapes.
· A visor slit instead of eyes, which reads as a small screen. Terminal, not arcade cabinet.
· A grounding shade on the bottom two rows and a highlight on the top-left arc, so they have form instead of being flat fills.
· Pupils track the cursor on a snapped 4px grid — they watch you before you ever press a key.

Personality now comes from three dome shapes and four skirt rhythms rather than from copying named characters. Twelve combinations, eight in use.

B1 · ANNOTATED CAPTURES

Real unretouched screenshots from the repo, framed and called out. Callouts point at regions of the frame, not at guessed pixel coordinates inside the image — that is deliberate, it survives a re-capture.

Cheapest to build, impossible to make misleading, and it never drifts. The weakness is that it is also the most ordinary.

B2 · GHOSTS AS WINDOWS

Your masks idea. The silhouettes are CSS masks over the real captures, so character and product occupy the same pixels. Hover one and the hue wash and visor fade out — the ghost dissolves and you are just looking at the app.

This is the one that solves two problems at once: the app is visible, and the mascot finally has a job. It is also the most distinctive thing on this page.

Watch for: the crop has to be chosen per capture or you get meaningless pixels inside a nice shape.

B3 · CLICKABLE REPLICA

Click any session in the sidebar — the pane follows. Rebuilt in HTML rather than captured, using the app's own font logic: sans for UI chrome, mono for the terminal pane.

This is the honest version of what Ghostties OS was trying to do. That board invented terminal content and presented it as the app; this one is explicitly a replica and says so on the board.

The cost is real: every release, someone has to re-measure this against the actual app or it quietly starts lying again. That is the whole tradeoff.

C1 · PIXEL MORPH

The ghost is generated from a formula rather than hand-drawn, so it can be resampled to any grid and still be the same shape. Four resolutions: 48, 24, 12, 6.

On the page each step is tied to a scroll beat, so nothing fades or slides — sections resolve. The transition comes out of the same lattice the icons are drawn on, which is about as on-brand as motion gets.

Loops here so you can see it; on the real page you drive it.

C2 · ANCHORED GHOST, FOCUS PULL

You said you hate scroll-jacking. This does not do it: sticky positioning plus an intersection observer, so the scrollbar keeps behaving normally the whole way down.

The ghost holds one position for the section. Copy blocks on the left blur and recede out of focus, one pulls sharp, and the capture under the ghost swaps to match. Three beats, three features.

Under reduced-motion the states swap instantly and nothing blurs.

C3 · CAST OF EIGHT

Each ghost owns exactly one capability and appears only where that capability does — in the docs, on the social card, in the changelog entry that shipped it.

The structural bit is the rule, not the names: if a feature has no ghost, it does not get a section. That keeps the page from sprawling as you ship.

Names are a strawman. PILOT, LANE, BEACON, EMBER, QUORUM, ECHO, DRIFT, ROOT. Say the word and I will run a proper naming pass — the old set was blinky/inky/pinky/clyde, which is the thing you are trying to get away from.

TYPE — the decision that settles the AI question

Three specimen sheets, same content in all three so they are actually comparable. None of them use Inter, Roboto or a system sans, which is the loudest tell.

Worth knowing before you pick: the app itself is SF Pro for UI chrome and SF Mono for the terminal — a sans plus a mono. T3 is that pairing with more character, so site and product would finally match. T1 is the furthest from anything a machine reaches for by default but also the furthest from the app. T2 has the widest range and the most risk.

The house rules are the same across all three, and they matter more than the fonts: square status marks, never circles or pills. Block labels butted together with shared hairlines, no rounded corners, no drop shadows on chrome. Uppercase micro-labels at 0.2em tracking. That vocabulary is what will read as designed.

CONTENT MAP

Ten sections. 02, 03 and 04 are the pitch — if someone reads only those they should already want it.

The gap worth flagging: section 08, first 60 seconds. Nothing on the site today says what happens after install, where it puts things, what it touches, or how to leave. For a terminal fork that is the single biggest unspoken objection, and it is cheap to answer.

Sections 05, 06 and 07 need captures that do not exist yet.

A · ARCADE — the winner. Developed on the Round 2 page.

This was the first pass: full Pac-Man DNA, maze grid, phosphor bloom, ghosts eating pellets. Kept here for comparison — round two backs off the maze, redraws the ghosts, and turns the game into an opt-in secret rather than the first thing you see.

B · GHOSTTIES OS — retired.

You were right: the terminal pane is invented content presented as the app, which makes the whole board a lie however good it looks. The idea survives on the Round 2 page as B3, rebuilt honestly and labelled as a replica.

C · SÉANCE — broken up for parts.

The quiet editorial dark did not survive, but four ideas out of it did: ghosts as masks, pixel-block morph, anchored ghosts with a focus pull, and one ghost per feature. All four are built on the Round 2 page.
